title: Periodic table of sound

rows.name: In
rows.deamer: Chion's on-screen sound, via Deamer p.167

rows.name: Off
rows.deamer: Chion's off-screen (acousmatic) sound, p.167; removing effects shrinks it, p.168

columns.name: Poet
columns.what: RY reading her own lines: the spring every other voice is measured from (poet_dist 1.0, f0 111 Hz).
columns.law: Owns the front. Never cut, never ducked, never covered: everything else yields to her.

links.why: a voice from outside the image makes the image something to read
links.deamer: TEXT: the optical AND sound image must be read (C2: 24, p.45). Sound is one of the five coordinates attacked (pp.163, 171). Chion's synchresis and contract are discussed here (pp.167-168). Enter the Void: one blank voice-over for speech and thought; 'whispers, blank voices, uterine soundscapes' (pp.338, 342).

links.why: a pure sound the image no longer answers
links.deamer: TEXT: pure actual sound situation, the actual sound image cut off from motor extension (pp.41-45, 138-145, 162). Deamer gives no separate definition, examples or sub-types. Five supplies the practice: talk swallowed by the waves' roar, the sea's white noise, near silence, the toads' crescendo (pp.302, 304). Chion's tactics (p.168) are Deamer's only account of HOW sound becomes time-image.

rows.IN: Her mouth seen saying it: the sound locks to a face; synchresis.
rows.OFF: Her voice from the next room of the scene: she is somewhere, unseen.
rows.OUT: Voice-over: she reads over the world, and the world is read.

columns.name: Whisper
columns.what: The poet's voice in fragments: 439 power-phrase chops and breaths, her words as material.
columns.law: Only in her silences (≥ 3.5 s gap), 18 s apart; never over a word of hers.

links.why: breath and voiced thought inside one body
links.deamer: TEXT: hearing with the character (p.13). Diving Bell: identification extends into the sound field, with the protagonist's thoughts as voice-over, breathing, and voices arriving in waves (pp.179-180). Internal subjective sound = point-of-audition anchored in one body.

rows.IN: A whisper matched to a moving mouth: someone in frame speaks with her voice.
rows.OFF: Her words half-heard behind the scene, as if remembered in the room.
rows.OUT: Her voice as texture over everything: interior, inside the head.

columns.name: Kin
columns.what: Mouths nearest the poet (poet_dist < 7.5): narration kin singing her lines.
columns.law: Waits for her line to end and ≥ 2 s of quiet; then answers. Drops to 0.12 if she returns.

links.why: two voices trading one text: a duel of lines (inference)
links.deamer: Marginal: a silent, empty shop floor opens Made in Dagenham (p.228). No theory.

rows.IN: A second speaker seen answering her: dialogue.
rows.OFF: An answer from beyond the frame: the scene has another person in it.
rows.OUT: A second narrator: the text is told twice.

columns.name: Mouth
columns.what: Other singers carrying her lines, further from the poet (dist ≥ 7.5), by register ABYSSAL / DEEP / LOW / HIGH.
columns.law: Same law as Kin, one step lower: never two mouths at once.

links.why: the same words in other mouths: her story told by others (inference)
links.deamer: Analogy only: the series of time is likened to serialism in music (p.44). Nothing on film sound.

rows.IN: A singer in shot mouthing her words: the musical, the number.
rows.OFF: Singing from somewhere in the world of the shot.
rows.OUT: Her poem sung over the film: the song as commentary.

columns.name: Chorus
columns.what: Many mouths at once: combined codex lines, the crowd singing the poem.
columns.law: Only in gaps and endings; the codas. A chorus under her is a collision.

links.why: the voice dispersed, no centre of hearing
links.deamer: TEXT: Naqoyqatsi (pp.186-188). Images vary against Glass's 'music-images' in nine movements; the sound has no human centre.

rows.IN: A crowd seen singing: the collective in frame.
rows.OFF: A crowd heard beyond the frame: the world is populated.
rows.OUT: A chorus over the image: the people who are missing, speaking.

columns.name: Found voice
columns.what: Strangers speaking in the archive footage: narrators, instructors, voices of the films themselves.
columns.law: An archive voice never speaks over hers: under her words it drops to 0.12; alone it may lead.

examples.label: Scatter radar: Space research from the ground
Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge

links.why: the found narrator: the everyday world explaining itself (inference)
links.deamer: TEXT (descriptive): A Screaming Man, with lingering silences, a pen scratching, 'diegetic sound prevails', sotto voce acting, war as background noise, and an unheard answer as ellipsis (pp.255-256).

rows.IN: The film's own speaker, lips in sync: the found film talking.
rows.OFF: The found film's narrator unseen: its world explains itself.
rows.OUT: An archive voice cut loose from its picture: found speech as quotation.

columns.name: Song
columns.what: Sections of the 34 carrier songs (744 segments, 19 families): the poem's own music.
columns.law: One music at a time. Under her voice: mid-band carved (−7 dB at 1.4 kHz), bus to 10%.

links.why: music covering every zone while voices hand the centre around
links.deamer: TEXT: Timecode, the audio 'fourth flow' (p.184). Music covers all zones while a mix spotlights one quadrant's voices and effects, so the centre is handed off by sound.

rows.IN: A band or radio seen playing it: source music.
rows.OFF: Music from a room nearby: the world has a party in it.
rows.OUT: Score: the song over the image.

columns.name: Loop
columns.what: Rhythm: 60 mined loops on a bar grid (median 2.56 s, flatness 0.008 — the most tonal thing in the atlas).
columns.law: Enters on a bar; matches tempo by playback rate; yields to any voice by carving, not stopping.

links.why: musicals: music as the movement of the world (Deamer p.125)
links.deamer: TEXT (Section II): musicals and dance films, where song and dance are natural to the world, are cases of the implied dream (p.125).

rows.IN: A machine seen repeating: the loop is its sound.
rows.OFF: A pulse from outside the frame: the world keeps time.
rows.OUT: A beat under the film: the cut is paced by it.

columns.name: Stem
columns.what: Orchestra chairs: single instruments from the songs (drums, piano, synth, vocals, bass, strings).
columns.law: A chair in the poem's key (root or fifth) may stay under her; other keys wait for the gap.

links.why: one instrument held like a face: an affect expressed (inference)
links.deamer: TEXT (Section III only): The Terrorist's close-ups approach silence with only breathing and ambient nature, or are swamped by synthetic strings (pp.189-190). Section II gives the affection-image no sound dimension.

columns.name: Found music
columns.what: Music inside the archive footage: scores, radios, bands of the found films.
columns.law: One music at a time: two musics crossfade on a beat, or the later one sinks to texture (lowpass, −12 dB).

links.why: source music moving the found world (Deamer p.125)
links.deamer: TEXT (Section II): musicals and dance films, where song and dance are natural to the world, are cases of the implied dream (p.125).

rows.OUT: The found film's score lifted onto another picture.

columns.name: Drone
columns.what: The unified drone: the corpus clock itself (1,440.1 s), and drone keynotes.
columns.law: Never leaves. Under her 0.045, in breaths 0.09, after her 0.13 (the water table's key-bed).

links.why: a pure sound that no longer extends into action
links.deamer: TEXT: pure actual sound situation, the actual sound image cut off from motor extension (pp.41-45, 138-145, 162). Deamer gives no separate definition, examples or sub-types. Five supplies the practice: talk swallowed by the waves' roar, the sea's white noise, near silence, the toads' crescendo (pp.302, 304). Chion's tactics (p.168) are Deamer's only account of HOW sound becomes time-image.

rows.IN: A hum whose source is seen: a machine, a fridge, a turbine.
rows.OFF: The hum of a place: the room tone of the world.
rows.OUT: The floor under the whole film: time itself sounding.

columns.name: Bed
columns.law: Keynote: ducks under every voice (1 − 0.9·amt, 30 ms down, 160 ms up).

rows.IN: Ambience with its source in view: the sea in the shot of the sea.
rows.OFF: The weather of the scene, unseen.
rows.OUT: A pad under the film: mood as floor.

columns.name: Texture
columns.what: Textures: 30 noisy segments (flatness 0.74, centroid 3.5 kHz — the noisiest element).
columns.law: Lowest priority of the field: first to go when two things fight.

links.why: matter as grain: perception broken into particles (inference)
links.deamer: TEXT: Naqoyqatsi (pp.186-188). Images vary against Glass's 'music-images' in nine movements; the sound has no human centre.

rows.IN: Grain with a visible cause: rain on glass.
rows.OFF: Static, wind, crowd murmur: the world as noise.
rows.OUT: Hiss, tape, surface noise: the medium sounding.

columns.name: Found noise
columns.what: Noise and effects in the archive footage: machines, traffic, rooms, weather.
columns.law: Normalised to −24 LUFS; ducks under voices; removing it shrinks the off-screen space (Deamer p.168).

links.why: remove the effects and the space off-screen closes (p.168)
links.deamer: TEXT: pure actual sound situation, the actual sound image cut off from motor extension (pp.41-45, 138-145, 162). Deamer gives no separate definition, examples or sub-types. Five supplies the practice: talk swallowed by the waves' roar, the sea's white noise, near silence, the toads' crescendo (pp.302, 304). rows.IN: The found film's effects, in sync: synchresis, the fourth dimension of the image.
rows.OFF: The found film's world heard beyond its frame.
rows.OUT: Effects laid on a picture that did not make them: the lock exposed.

columns.name: Riser
columns.law: Aims at a cut: ends on the next cut or breath; never rises into her word.

links.why: a line of tension toward the next image (inference)

rows.IN: A visible thing gathering: engine spinning up.
rows.OUT: Tension laid over the cut: the edit announced.

columns.name: Hit
columns.law: Snaps to the next silence ≥ 1 s within 3 s; at least 7 s apart; never on a word.

links.why: a sound as the index of an event it does not show (inference)
links.deamer: TEXT (descriptive only): Mother opens on wind in grass, then tablas, guitar and strings as the woman dances 'to music only she can hear' (pp.213-214). Not theorised.

rows.IN: An impact seen and heard at once: the index.
rows.OFF: A bang off-screen: an event the frame did not catch.
rows.OUT: A stinger on the cut: the edit hits.

columns.name: Silence
columns.what: The gap: her 606 breaths and pauses, and the archive's silent shots. The zero of the table.
columns.law: Silence is placed, not left: the one element nothing may enter unless the law allows it.

links.why: Five: talk drowned by waves, then near-silence building (pp.302–304)
links.deamer: TEXT: pure actual sound situation, the actual sound image cut off from motor extension (pp.41-45, 138-145, 162). Deamer gives no separate definition, examples or sub-types. Five supplies the practice: talk swallowed by the waves' roar, the sea's white noise, near silence, the toads' crescendo (pp.302, 304). Chion's tactics (p.168) are Deamer's only account of HOW sound becomes time-image.

rows.IN: A silent shot: the picture without its sound.
rows.OUT: The film stops speaking: the time-image's zero.

laws.name: One clock
laws.rule: Everything sits on the 24:00 suite clock; nothing is re-timed by the mix.

laws.name: Her voice untouched
laws.rule: The poet is never cut, ducked or covered.

laws.name: One speaker
laws.rule: Voices never overlap: a lower voice waits for her line to end and ≥ 2 s of quiet, or it is held.

laws.name: One music
laws.rule: Two musics never play at the front together: the later crossfades in on a beat or sinks to texture.

laws.name: Carve, don't bury
laws.rule: Under a voice, music and field lose the mid band (−7 dB at 1.4 kHz, Q 0.7) and drop to 10%, 30 ms down, 160 ms up.

laws.name: Snap to breath
laws.rule: Hits and risers land in silences ≥ 1 s, at least 7 s apart.

laws.name: Level
laws.rule: Archive sound is normalised toward −24 LUFS; nothing jumps.

laws.name: Silence is placed
laws.rule: A gap is an element: leave it empty on purpose.

moves.name: Drop the score
moves.does: remove the music: the image loses its instructions

moves.name: Drop the effects
moves.does: remove the noise: the off-screen space closes

moves.name: Unnatural voice
moves.does: theatrical, text-heavy, swamped or unsubtitled speech: the voice stops belonging to a body

moves.name: Expose the lock
moves.does: put a sound IN against a picture that did not make it: synchresis shown as a contract
